name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [master]
    # A PR that only touches docs or top-level markdown never affects the
    # compiler, runtime, or tests; skip CI for it entirely.
    paths-ignore:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '*.md'

# One run per branch at a time: a push that supersedes a queued or running
# run cancels it. Every run was 13 jobs against a small runner pool, and a
# busy afternoon queued 22 master runs and several per PR branch, so a
# result arrived hours late; only the newest commit of a branch matters.
#
# On master a running run is left to finish: the macOS lane runs there only
# (see the posix matrix), and its queue is long, so cancelling on every push
# left no master run with a finished macOS job (five pushes in a row on
# 2026-09-30). A push that arrives meanwhile waits as the group's one
# pending run, which a newer push replaces, so master still tests its
# newest commit next.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  # Every lane runs the whole corpus in one job. The Linux/gcc lane used to
  # split it into two slices (make's TEST_SHARD=k/n), which shortened that
  # lane's wall time; but with dozens of PRs open at once the runner pool,
  # not a job's length, set the latency, and the extra job per run only
  # lengthened the queue. TEST_SHARD stays in the make call (1/1 picks the
  # whole corpus) so a lane can be split again by changing its nshards.
  # Slice 1 of each lane carries the C-side test legs, the property gates,
  # the benchmarks and optcarrot.
  posix:
    # The slice shows in the name only when the corpus is split.
    name: ${{ matrix.os }} / ${{ matrix.cc }}${{ matrix.nshards > 1 && format(' ({0}/{1})', matrix.shard, matrix.nshards) || '' }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # A pull request runs one job: the clang lane, the whole corpus at -O0.
      # A PR is checked where the maintainer's own gate (gcc, with the
      # property gates, benchmarks and optcarrot) is not, and every lane --
      # gcc, clang, macOS, -m32 and wasm -- runs again on the merge commit,
      # which is where the rest is caught and fixed. With a few dozen PRs
      # open at once the runner pool, not a job's length, set the latency,
      # and each PR held four jobs of it. The macOS runners are the fewest,
      # so that lane stays on master pushes (its queue was 16 minutes at the
      # median and over an hour at the tail when every PR ran it).
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(github.event_name == 'push' && '[{"os":"ubuntu-latest","cc":"gcc","shard":1,"nshards":1},{"os":"ubuntu-latest","cc":"clang","shard":1,"nshards":1},{"os":"macos-latest","cc":"clang","shard":1,"nshards":1}]' || '[{"os":"ubuntu-latest","cc":"clang","shard":1,"nshards":1}]') }}
    env:
      # `sccache <cc>` wrapper. sccache forwards through to the
      # underlying compiler when its cache misses, so this stays
      # transparent. The test/bench rules use separate compile and
      # link steps so the compile step is in sccache's cacheable
      # pattern; the test compile also loads a precompiled
      # spinel_rt.h (see PCH_ROOT in the Makefile), which cuts the
      # compile even when sccache misses. sccache hashes the
      # preprocessed source, so the gcc-implicit .gch never leaks
      # into the cache key; for clang's -include-pch sccache
      # declines to cache and forwards, which still gets the PCH
      # speedup.
      #
      # The store is sccache's own on-disk cache, carried between
      # runs as ONE actions/cache entry per lane and slice (the
      # steps below), not the GitHub cache service as sccache's
      # backend (SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED). That backend makes a service
      # round trip per compile, and with twelve jobs each running
      # four compiles a second the service answered "rate limit
      # exceeded" to about half of them (run 35706592343): reads
      # that fail are misses, writes that fail never land, and the
      # corpus slices settled at a 35-75% hit rate. A restored disk
      # cache answers every lookup locally.
      CC: sccache ${{ matrix.cc }}
      SCCACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.sccache
      SCCACHE_STARTUP_TIMEOUT: "30"
      # Keep the server alive across steps. See the pre-start step below.
      SCCACHE_IDLE_TIMEOUT: "0"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Set up sccache
        uses: mozilla-actions/sccache-action@v0.0.10

      # The key never matches (it carries the run id), so the post step
      # always saves this run's cache; the restore key picks up the newest
      # earlier one for the same lane and slice, from this branch or from
      # master. Old entries fall to the repository's cache eviction.
      - name: Restore the sccache store
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .sccache
          key: sccache-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.cc }}-${{ matrix.shard }}-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: sccache-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.cc }}-${{ matrix.shard }}-

      # Start the server once here so `make -j` clients don't race to start it.
      - name: Pre-start sccache server
        run: sccache --start-server

      - name: Set up Ruby
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: "4.0"

      # coreutils is NOT preinstalled on the macOS runners, so `timeout` and
      # `gtimeout` were both absent and the whole suite ran with no time limit:
      # one hanging test held the job until GitHub's six-hour cap instead of
      # failing in ten seconds. Installing it is what makes the per-test
      # timeout real; the PATH line then gives the GNU names.
      - name: Install GNU coreutils (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: brew install coreutils
      - name: Expose GNU coreutils on PATH (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Fetch libprism sources
        run: make deps

      - name: Build (parse + regexp + spinelc)
        run: make -j$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) all

      - name: Run tests
        # Opt level is compiler-specific -- they behave oppositely on the
        # spinel_rt.h-heavy per-test TUs (800+ static fns):
        #   gcc:   -O1 prunes unreferenced statics + DCEs before the costly
        #          codegen, so -O1 compiles faster than -O0 (0.54 vs 0.94 s a
        #          file on 2026-10-05; the header was far smaller when this
        #          was first measured at 2.7 vs 25 ms).
        #   clang: -O1 still runs the full optimizer over every emitted inline
        #          static, so -O1 is ~2.5x SLOWER than -O0 (213 vs 88ms/file).
        # So gcc builds tests at -O1 and clang at -O0. Correctness is opt-level
        # independent (tests diff output, not codegen), and the gcc -O1 leg still
        # exercises the optimizing path; the clang leg's job is that clang accepts
        # the emitted C and runs it, which -O0 covers.
        # The `CC=gcc` / `CC=clang` here does NOT take sccache off the
        # per-test compiles, although 970112c6 meant it to: common.mk
        # re-wraps a command-line CC with `override CC := sccache $(CC)`
        # whenever sccache is on PATH, and the stats step below shows the
        # result (91% hits, 1479 of 1621 executed compiles, on run
        # 35701579214's gcc slice 1). That is what makes a slice run in
        # ~120 s: the same slice compiled cold costs ~370 s, which is what
        # the -m32 lane paid until it got the same wrapper. The override
        # is kept as the spelling of the opt level per compiler; NO_CCACHE=1
        # would be the way to actually unwrap.
        #
        # The gcc lane runs one eighth of the corpus, a different eighth each
        # run (the run number picks it), beside the C-side legs. The whole
        # corpus under gcc is what `make gate` runs before every push to
        # master, so the lane repeated it, and it had become the slowest job
        # by far: 45 minutes of a 51-minute job on run 37272572814. Nearly
        # every push touches lib/spinel_rt.h, which every test's C includes,
        # so sccache missed on 96% of 6,366 compiles, and gcc takes about
        # 0.5 s a file on this header where clang -O0 takes 0.08 s (1.4 s on
        # the runner). The clang lanes and the -m32 lane still run every
        # test; the eighth keeps a different gcc than the maintainer's own
        # in the loop.
        run: |
          shard="${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ matrix.nshards }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.cc }}" = gcc ]; then shard="$(( GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER % 8 + 1 ))/8"; fi
          # the Linux clang lane on a master push: a quarter, rotating. The maintainer's own
          # pre-push lanes (clang, clang -m32, wasm32 on a separate machine) run the whole
          # corpus before every push, so this lane was repeating them (2026-10-07); a pull
          # request still runs all of it.
          if [ "${{ matrix.cc }}" = clang ] && [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = ubuntu-latest ] && [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = push ]; then shard="$(( GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER % 4 + 1 ))/4"; fi
          # macOS on a master push: a rotating quarter plus every test whose answer depends on the
          # operating system (tools/os_sensitive.re: time, files, processes, signals, sockets, threads,
          # the GC, FFI) and the packages' tests, which is where its failures have been. It was the
          # whole corpus, 20 of the run's 21 minutes. Add a pattern to the file when a test fails here
          # alone and the pattern would have kept it in.
          always=""
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = macos-latest ] && [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = push ]; then
            shard="$(( GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER % 4 + 1 ))/4"
            always="TEST_ALWAYS=tools/os_sensitive.re"
          fi
          echo "corpus slice: $shard $always"
          make -j$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) ${{ matrix.shard == 1 && 'test' || 'test-corpus' }} TEST_SHARD=$shard $always ${{ matrix.cc == 'clang' && 'OPT=-O0 CC=clang' || 'OPT=-O1 CC=gcc' }}

      # spin's end-to-end check: it builds real projects, which a clean
      # checkout on another machine is worth seeing. Linux/gcc only.
      #
      # alloc-report-test, infer-test and scale-test ran here too. What they
      # read is the generated C and a count of the front end's work, neither
      # of which depends on the machine or the C compiler, and `make gate`
      # runs all three before every push to master (gate-props), so the lane
      # only repeated an answer already known: about 3.5 minutes a run. They
      # were put here when the pre-push gate did not include them (an Int-
      # keyed hash lost its typed variant for weeks with CI green); it has
      # since.
      - name: Run spin's end-to-end check
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.cc == 'gcc' && matrix.shard == 1
        run: make spin-check

      # Benchmark integration test. Compiles every benchmark/*.rb through
      # the full pipeline (cc -Werror) and diffs the output against CRuby.
      # The bench programs are larger and more realistic than the test/*.rb
      # fixtures, so they exercise object-graph shapes (cons cells, tree
      # nodes, linked structures) that `make test` misses -- a holder
      # specialization regression once slipped past test + optcarrot
      # precisely because bench wasn't gated. Linux/gcc only: the output
      # is deterministic across compilers/OS, and the gcc job's test step
      # runs well under the clang jobs' (sccache covers more of its
      # compiles), so it carries both bench and optcarrot to keep the
      # slowest job -- which sets the CI wall time -- the clang test run.
      - name: Run benchmark integration test
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.cc == 'gcc' && matrix.shard == 1
        run: make bench

      # End-to-end optcarrot integration test.  Linux only -- no
      # value in repeating it across compilers / on macOS, since
      # the codegen output is the same and the runtime cost
      # (~10s) is the same too.  Catches regressions in the
      # `pack-for-spinel.rb` flow + Lan_Master.nes checksum 59662
      # contract that the standalone `make test` doesn't cover.
      - name: Run optcarrot integration test
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.cc == 'gcc' && matrix.shard == 1
        run: make optcarrot

      - name: sccache stats
        if: always()
        run: sccache --show-stats

  # A 32-bit target. sp_int is the pointer width (lib/sp_types.h), so a
  # -m32 build is the one place the runtime's and the emitters' word-size
  # assumptions are exercised: a `1 << 40` that is UB there, a `%d` fed a
  # long long, a 16GB slab reservation, a literal past the target's Integer.
  # It is also the rehearsal for wasm32. The corpus only: the C-side legs
  # (the CRuby extension test, the rbs tooling) have no 32-bit toolchain to
  # build against, and a test that assumes a 64-bit Integer says
  # `# spinel: int64` in its first line and is filtered out (Makefile,
  # SPINEL_INT_BITS). Every generated program links -lcrypt, hence the
  # i386 libcrypt; gcc-multilib brings the 32-bit libc and libgcc.
  #
  # sccache, exactly as the posix lanes have it. Without it this lane
  # compiled every per-test TU cold and its corpus slice took 370 s where
  # the gcc lane's took 120 s (run 35701579214 on #4797): the -m32 compile
  # itself costs the same as the 64-bit one (measured locally, cold, both
  # 148 s for the same slice), the whole difference was the cache. The
  # -m32 flag is part of sccache's key, so this lane's entries never
  # collide with the 64-bit gcc lane's.
  #
  # master pushes only, not pull requests. A commit that changes the runtime
  # headers, or codegen every program goes through, misses sccache for the
  # whole corpus, and the one-job lane then compiles all ~4500 programs on four
  # vCPUs: 27 minutes, against 3 on a warm cache. Every PR waited on that. A
  # word-size break a PR brings is found on its merge commit instead, and
  # fixed there; splitting the lane into slices would halve it but take one
  # more runner per run, which is what queues the pool when pushes cluster.
  linux32:
    name: ubuntu-latest / clang -m32
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # A hung apt-get in the toolchain step held this job for over four
    # hours on 2026-10-01, and with it the master concurrency group: every
    # later push waited as the group's pending run. The lane takes about
    # 20 minutes.
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      CC: sccache clang -m32
      SCCACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.sccache
      SCCACHE_STARTUP_TIMEOUT: "30"
      SCCACHE_IDLE_TIMEOUT: "0"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Set up sccache
        uses: mozilla-actions/sccache-action@v0.0.10

      - name: Restore the sccache store
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .sccache
          key: sccache-ubuntu-latest-clang-m32-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: sccache-ubuntu-latest-clang-m32-

      - name: Pre-start sccache server
        run: sccache --start-server

      - name: Set up Ruby
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: "4.0"

      - name: Install the 32-bit toolchain
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: |
          sudo dpkg --add-architecture i386
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y gcc-multilib libc6-dev-i386 libcrypt-dev:i386

      - name: Fetch libprism sources
        run: make deps

      - name: Build (parse + regexp + spinelc), 32-bit
        run: make -j$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) all

      # clang -O0: the lane checks word-size assumptions, not what an
      # optimizer makes of them, and the corpus is all compile time. Nearly
      # every push misses sccache for the whole corpus (the runtime header
      # changed), and on that header gcc -m32 -Og takes 0.34 s a file where
      # clang -m32 -O0 with its precompiled header takes 0.10 s; an eighth
      # of the corpus ran in 32 s against 14 s on 16 cores (2026-10-05).
      # Under gcc the lane took 26 to 28 minutes of a run.
      # A quarter of the corpus per push, rotating by run number: the maintainer's pre-push
      # -m32 lane runs the whole corpus (2026-10-07), so this one repeated it in 9 minutes.
      - name: Run the test corpus as 32-bit programs
        run: |
          shard="$(( GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER % 4 + 1 ))/4"
          echo "corpus slice: $shard"
          make -j$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) test-corpus OPT=-O0 TEST_SHARD=$shard

      - name: sccache stats
        if: always()
        run: sccache --show-stats

  # wasm32-wasi. Two commits in eight days left `--target=wasm32-wasi` unable
  # to link any program (64cd200e's execv, 9d8f098f's getrlimit), and both
  # were reported from outside the repo a day after the merge, because no lane
  # builds for this target: linux32 is the word-size rehearsal, not the wasm
  # one, and a wasm-only link error passes straight through it. The shape is
  # always the same -- lib/wasi/*.h declares a POSIX function, sp_wasi.c never
  # defines it, and nothing notices until something first calls it, which
  # docs/wasm.md's own invariant forbids ("never as a link error"). The
  # existing `make wasm-test` builds seven corpus programs for the target and
  # diffs them against their expected output, which catches the whole class
  # (#4807).
  #
  # The sdk is a 183 MB download, so it is cached by version; the engine is
  # wasmtime, installed from its release tarball. WASM_ENGINE_REQUIRED makes a
  # missing engine fail rather than skip, so this job cannot report success by
  # doing nothing.
  wasm:
    name: wasm32-wasi
    # master pushes only, as the -m32 and macOS lanes: a PR runs the clang
    # lane alone (see the matrix above)
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # docs/wasm.md asks for 34 or later (the exnref lowering)
      WASI_SDK_VERSION: "34"
      # docs/wasm.md: wasmtime 48 runs the modules as they are emitted
      WASMTIME_VERSION: "49.0.0"
      WASI_SDK_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/.wasi-sdk
      CC: sccache cc
      SCCACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.sccache
      SCCACHE_STARTUP_TIMEOUT: "30"
      SCCACHE_IDLE_TIMEOUT: "0"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Set up sccache
        uses: mozilla-actions/sccache-action@v0.0.10

      - name: Restore the sccache store
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .sccache
          key: sccache-wasm-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: sccache-wasm-

      - name: Pre-start sccache server
        run: sccache --start-server

      - name: Set up Ruby
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: "4.0"

      - name: Restore the wasi-sdk
        id: wasi-sdk-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .wasi-sdk
          key: wasi-sdk-${{ env.WASI_SDK_VERSION }}-x86_64-linux

      - name: Install the wasi-sdk
        if: steps.wasi-sdk-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: |
          v=${WASI_SDK_VERSION}
          url="https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasi-sdk/releases/download/wasi-sdk-${v}/wasi-sdk-${v}.0-x86_64-linux.tar.gz"
          curl -fsSL "$url" -o /tmp/wasi-sdk.tar.gz
          mkdir -p .wasi-sdk
          tar -xzf /tmp/wasi-sdk.tar.gz -C .wasi-sdk --strip-components=1

      - name: Install wasmtime
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/releases/download/v${WASMTIME_VERSION}/wasmtime-v${WASMTIME_VERSION}-x86_64-linux.tar.xz -o /tmp/wasmtime.tar.xz
          mkdir -p /tmp/wasmtime && tar -xJf /tmp/wasmtime.tar.xz -C /tmp/wasmtime --strip-components=1
          echo "/tmp/wasmtime" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Fetch libprism sources
        run: make deps

      - name: Build (parse + regexp + spinelc)
        run: make -j$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) all

      - name: Build the wasm32-wasi runtime and run the wasm programs
        run: make -j$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) wasm-test WASM_ENGINE_REQUIRED=1

      - name: sccache stats
        if: always()
        run: sccache --show-stats

name: Gate trailer

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    branches: [master]

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: gate-trailer-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: "4.0"

      - name: Verify the head commit's Gate trailer
        id: verify
        env:
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.clone_url }}
        run: |
          # GitHub creates refs/pull/N/head shortly after the pull request opens, and
          # this job can start before it exists. Retry it, then fetch the head commit
          # from the pull request's own repository.
          for wait in 0 5 10 20; do
            sleep "$wait"
            git fetch --no-tags --quiet origin "refs/pull/$PR/head" && break
          done
          if ! git cat-file -e "$HEAD_SHA^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
            git fetch --no-tags --quiet "$HEAD_REPO" "$HEAD_SHA"
          fi
          set +e
          out=$(ruby tools/gate.rb verify "$HEAD_SHA" 2>&1)
          rc=$?
          set -e
          echo "$out"
          printf '### Gate trailer\n\n~~~\n%s\n~~~\n' "$out" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          case $rc in
            0) label="gate: verified" ;;
            1) label="gate: mismatch" ;;
            2) label="gate: no trailer" ;;
            *) label="gate: unknown master" ;;
          esac
          echo "label=$label" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Label the pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          LABEL: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.label }}
        run: |
          present=$(gh api "repos/$GH_REPO/issues/$PR/labels" --jq '.[].name')
          while IFS='|' read -r name color desc; do
            gh label create "$name" --color "$color" --description "$desc" --force
            if [ "$name" != "$LABEL" ] && grep -qxF "$name" <<<"$present"; then
              gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GH_REPO/issues/$PR/labels/$(jq -rn --arg l "$name" '$l|@uri')" >/dev/null
            fi
          done <<'EOF'
          gate: verified|0e8a16|The head commit's Gate trailer names the tree its merge with master gives
          gate: mismatch|d73a4a|The head commit's Gate trailer names a tree its merge with master does not give
          gate: no trailer|cfd3d7|The head commit carries no Gate trailer
          gate: unknown master|fbca04|The Gate trailer names a master commit this repository does not have
          EOF
          gh api -X POST "repos/$GH_REPO/issues/$PR/labels" -f "labels[]=$LABEL" >/dev/null

name: ci
'on':
  - push
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-20.04
    strategy:
      matrix:
        compiler:
          - gcc
          - clang
    steps:
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: 'sudo apt install -q ${{ matrix.compiler }} libgc-dev'
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v1
      - name: Build and test
        run: 'make test CC=${{ matrix.compiler }}'

name: ❄️ Lint

on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  markdownlint:
    name: 🍶 Markdown
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: 🚀 Use Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v2.1.4
        with:
          node-version: '12.x'
      - run: npm install -g markdownlint-cli@0.25.0
      - run: markdownlint '**/*.md' --ignore node_modules
  shellcheck:
    name: 🥂 Shell
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: 🧹 ShellCheck
        uses: ludeeus/action-shellcheck@master
  trailing-whitespace:
    name: 🧋 Trailing whitespace
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: 🧹 Check for trailing whitespace
        run: |
          cd utils || exit
          sh ./check-for-trailing-whitespace.sh || exit 1
  yamllint:
    name: 🍺 YAML
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v2
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'  # Version range or exact version of a Python version to use, using SemVer's version range syntax
          architecture: 'x64'  # optional x64 or x86. Defaults to x64 if not specified
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install yamllint
      - name: 🧹 YAML Lint
        run: |
          # return non-zero exit code on warnings
